summary:
We developed The Lunatics, an interactive 3D space survival game designed to make STEM education more engaging and accessible.
Players become astronauts on a lunar mission, selecting essential supplies within a limited cargo capacity. After landing on the Moon, their spacecraft is destroyed, leaving them stranded. To survive 30 days until rescue, players must manage oxygen, food, water, and energy, repair critical systems, and avoid solar radiation. The game offers solo and cooperative modes and integrates real solar activity observations through NASA's DONKI API.
Our project addresses the challenge by transforming abstract scientific concepts into practical, interactive experiences. Players learn about resource management, engineering, physics, and teamwork through decisions that directly affect their survival.
The Lunatics is important because it connects classroom knowledge with space exploration, inspiring young people to develop critical thinking, problem-solving skills, and an interest in science and technology.
details:
1. What does your project do, and how does it work?

The Lunatics is an interactive 3D educational game that transforms science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) concepts into an exciting lunar survival mission.

Players take on the role of astronauts traveling to the Moon. The mission begins with a critical engineering decision: selecting essential supplies while respecting a 12 kg cargo limit. Players must choose between oxygen, food, water, equipment, and other items, knowing that every kilogram matters.

After piloting the spacecraft and landing on the Moon, an accident destroys the original rocket, leaving the astronauts stranded and without communication.

To survive, players must:

  • Manage limited oxygen, food, water, and energy.
  • Repair four essential systems by completing interactive challenges.
  • Avoid dangerous solar radiation zones and survive solar storms.
  • Make strategic decisions about resource consumption and replenishment.
  • Complete daily objectives before sleeping.
  • Survive 30 lunar mission days until a rescue spacecraft arrives.

The game offers Solo Mode, Local Cooperative Mode (with another player or a computer-controlled companion), and Online Cooperative Mode, allowing two astronauts to work together.

2. What benefits does your project offer?

Our project makes scientific learning more engaging by allowing players to experience the consequences of their decisions.

Instead of simply studying theoretical concepts, students apply them in simulated situations involving:

  • Physics: Spaceflight, gravity, movement, and spacecraft navigation.
  • Mathematics: Resource calculations, quantities, time management, and optimization.
  • Engineering: Equipment maintenance, system reliability, and problem-solving.
  • Science: Solar radiation, oxygen consumption, life-support systems, and lunar exploration.
  • Teamwork: Communication, cooperation, and shared decision-making.

The game encourages critical thinking, creativity, strategic planning, and the ability to solve problems under pressure.

3. What is the intended impact of your project?

Our main objective is to make space science and engineering more accessible, especially to teenagers and young adults.

Many students perceive science as a collection of abstract formulas disconnected from everyday experiences. The Lunatics addresses this challenge by transforming theoretical knowledge into interactive decisions.

Through the game, students can understand that successful space exploration depends on balancing competing demands, managing risks, and making informed decisions.

We envision developing the project into an educational resource that schools can use to complement classroom learning, encouraging students to pursue careers in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics.

Because the prototype runs in a web browser, it can be accessed on computers and compatible mobile devices without requiring expensive equipment.

4. What tools, programming languages, hardware, and software were used?

The current prototype was developed using web technologies and chatgpt:

HTML5 - Game interface and structure

CSS3 - Visual design and responsive layouts

JavaScript - Gameplay logic, controls, challenges, and resource management

WebGL - Real-time 3D graphics and lunar environments

Cloud-based server technology - Online multiplayer communication

D1 / SQL database - Multiplayer room synchronization and chat messages

NASA DONKI API - Access to real solar flare observations

The game includes a custom lightweight graphics engine and can run directly in modern web browsers.

NASA Data Integration

Our prototype includes a connection to NASA's DONKI (Space Weather Database of Notifications, Knowledge, Information) API.

Players can consult real observations of solar flares, connecting the simulated lunar environment with actual space weather information.

Currently, these observations are displayed in an informational panel. Future development aims to connect additional NASA datasets directly to gameplay mechanics, making mission conditions more scientifically dynamic.

5. What is the creative aspect of your project?

The creativity behind The Lunatics lies in combining an immersive survival adventure with educational engineering challenges.

Unlike traditional educational games that rely primarily on questions and answers, our project makes scientific concepts part of the gameplay itself.

For example, players must decide whether to carry additional oxygen, food, or equipment before leaving Earth. Once on the Moon, those choices directly affect their chances of survival.

The game also introduces daily maintenance challenges, limited replenishment opportunities, environmental hazards, and a rescue objective that requires players to survive 30 mission days.

These mechanics transform abstract concepts such as resource optimization, risk management, and system reliability into meaningful experiences.

The cooperative modes encourage players to communicate and divide responsibilities, creating opportunities for teamwork and collaborative learning.

6. What factors did your team consider during development?

Our team focused on six important factors:

  1. Educational value: Making scientific concepts understandable through interactive experiences.
  2. Scientific plausibility: Incorporating relevant principles of space exploration while simplifying complex physics for younger audiences.
  3. Accessibility: Developing a browser-based experience that does not require specialized gaming equipment.
  4. Engagement: Combining exploration, survival, challenges, and cooperative gameplay to maintain player motivation.
  5. Decision-making: Ensuring that choices about cargo, resources, and repairs have meaningful consequences.
  6. Scalability: Designing a prototype that can evolve to include additional NASA datasets, improved graphics, new challenges, and educational applications.

Final Project Statement

Our mission is to transform scientific knowledge into an experience that students can explore, understand, and remember.

The Lunatics is more than a space survival game. It is an educational experience that challenges players to think like engineers, make decisions like astronauts, and collaborate like real space mission teams.

By combining interactive gameplay, engineering challenges, and real NASA observations, we aim to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space explorers.

In future updates, we plan to expand the game's scientific accuracy and educational value by integrating additional NASA and Canadian Space Agency resources:

  • NASA RadLab: Real radiation measurements will help calibrate radiation exposure risks and improve shielding and protection mechanics.
  • NASA OSDR: Space biology research will support more realistic simulations of how sleep deprivation, nutrition, and prolonged space exposure affect astronaut health.
  • CSA — Food Production: Educational resources will inspire new challenges involving food cultivation, sustainable agriculture, and resource management in lunar habitats.

These planned integrations will bring the game closer to real space exploration challenges, connecting scientific research with meaningful gameplay decisions.

Our long-term vision is to develop The Lunatics into an accessible educational platform that helps students understand the complexities of living beyond Earth while encouraging innovation, teamwork, and critical thinking.
